name: Vex Ironhand
equipment: An insignia of rank (Sergeant, Ironshield Brigade)
A folded piece of parchment listing 47 names
A chunk of fire giant slag-iron (trophy)
features: Fighting Style: Defense (while wearing armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC; already included in AC of 19 = 16 chain mail + 2 shield + 1 Defense)
Second Wind (on your turn, use a bonus action to regain 1d10 + 5 hit points; usable once per short or long rest)
Action Surge (on your turn, you can take one additional action; usable once per short or long rest)
Extra Attack (you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn)
Martial Archetype: Battle Master — Superiority Dice (4d8 per short or long rest, DC 14 for maneuver saves)

Battle Master Maneuver: Trip Attack (when you hit with a weapon attack, expend one superiority die to add it to damage and force the target to make a STR save vs DC 14 or be knocked prone; target must be Large or smaller)

Battle Master Maneuver: Riposte (when a creature misses you with a melee attack, use your reaction and expend one superiority die to make a melee weapon attack; on hit, add the superiority die to damage)
Battle Master Maneuver: Precision Attack (when you make a weapon attack roll, expend one superiority die and add it to the roll; can use before or after the attack roll but before knowing if it hits)

Battle Master Maneuver: Menacing Attack (when you hit with a weapon attack, expend one superiority die to add it to damage and force the target to make a WIS save vs DC 14 or be frightened of you until end of your next turn)
Dwarven Resilience (advantage on saving throws against poison, and resistance to poison damage)
Stonecunning (whenever you make an INT (History) check related to the origin of stonework, you are considered proficient and add double your proficiency bonus instead of normal)
Dwarven Armor Training (Mountain Dwarf — proficiency with light and medium armor)
Dwarven Combat Training (proficiency with battleaxe, handaxe, light hammer, and warhammer)
Military Rank (Soldier feature — soldiers loyal to your former military organization still recognize your authority and influence; you can invoke your rank to exert influence over other soldiers)

personality.traits: I can stare down a fire giant without flinching — I have done it, in chains, for months. I keep a mental tally of debts, both owed and owing, and I never forget either. Every morning I recite the names on my list, all forty-seven, because if I forget them then no one in the world remembers they existed.
personality.ideals: Duty comes before comfort, before glory, and before death. I was given a command — hold the line — and I will hold it until the last name on my list is accounted for. The law is what separates soldiers from murderers, and I will not cross that line, no matter what the giants have done.
personality.bonds: Forty-seven dwarves of the Ironshield Brigade are enslaved in the Cinderworks, the fire giant fortress. I escaped alone and I carry their names on a piece of parchment that I will not lose, burn, or surrender. I owe them a rescue, and I will pay that debt or die in the attempt.
personality.flaws: I do not trust giants. Any of them. I have heard the arguments about 'good giants' and 'the Vaunting' and 'alliance,' and I think they are fairy tales told by people who have never been chained to an anvil. My cynicism makes me a difficult ally in a campaign that may require diplomacy with giant-kind.

appearance: Vex Ironhand is built like the fortress he once defended — four feet six inches of compact, unyielding stone-hard muscle, with shoulders broad enough to block a doorway and hands that look like they were carved from granite. His skin is the ruddy brown of old copper, weathered and scarred from decades of military service and months of fire giant captivity. His beard — once the pride of any proper dwarf, braided with iron rings marking campaigns served — is now cropped short and uneven, hacked off during his escape from the Cinderworks when a fire giant grabbed it. He has not grown it back, and other dwarves find this unsettling. His eyes are dark brown, nearly black, and they have the flat, evaluating quality of a veteran who has learned to assess threats before exchanging pleasantries. A lattice of burn scars covers his forearms and the backs of his hands — marks from the forges of the Cinderworks, where fire giant overseers thought nothing of letting molten slag splash on their slaves. His left ear is missing its upper half, taken by a fire giant's backhand that also broke his jaw in two places; the jaw healed crooked, giving his face a slightly lopsided set that makes his rare smiles look more like grimaces. He wears his chain mail with the practiced ease of someone who sleeps in armor, and his shield bears the device of the Ironshield Brigade — a closed fist gripping a hammer, though the paint is chipped and faded. A pair of manacles hangs from his belt, taken from the Cinderworks. He says they are a reminder. Other people think they are a promise.
backstory:
The Ironshield Brigade was not famous. They were a garrison unit, sixty dwarves assigned to hold Stoneshaft Keep, a minor fortress controlling a mountain pass in the Ashfell Mountains. It was not glamorous work. No bards sang about holding a pass that nobody tried to cross. But Sergeant Vex Ironhand did not need glamor — he needed order, discipline, and the quiet satisfaction of a job done properly.

Vex had served in the Brigade for thirty-two years when the fire giants came. He had joined at forty (young, for a dwarf), risen to Sergeant by sixty, and settled into the comfortable assumption that he would serve until retirement and then spend his remaining centuries complaining about the new recruits. He was good at his job in the way that unexceptional people can be good at things: through stubbornness, attention to detail, and an absolute refusal to cut corners.

The fire giants arrived without warning. A war band, forty strong, marching south from the peaks with purpose that the dwarves had never seen in giants before. They were not raiding — they were conquering, systematically, as though following a plan. Stoneshaft Keep held for three days. Vex was proud of that. Sixty dwarves against forty fire giants, and they held for three days. On the fourth morning, the giants breached the gate, and it was over in an hour.

They killed thirteen dwarves in the fighting. The remaining forty-seven, including Vex, they took alive. Not out of mercy — out of practicality. Fire giants need smiths, and dwarves are the best smiths in the world.

The Cinderworks was a nightmare forged in iron and lit by magma. The fire giant fortress was a massive forge-complex buried in a volcanic mountain, and the giants were building something — a great weapon, Vex thought, though he never saw enough to be certain. The dwarves were chained to anvils and put to work. Those who refused were beaten. Those who worked too slowly were burned. Those who tried to escape were made examples of, in ways that Vex does not discuss.

Vex survived for four months by doing what he had always done: enduring. He memorized the patrol routes. He noted the shift changes. He mapped the ventilation shafts in his head. And when the opportunity came — a supply delivery that left one gate understaffed for eleven minutes — he took it.

He escaped alone. That was not the plan. The plan had been to take everyone, but the window was too small and the route too narrow, and when the alarm sounded he had to choose between going back for the others and reaching the surface. He chose the surface. He tells himself it was the tactical decision — that a dead rescuer saves no one — but the guilt has not diminished in the months since.

He carries a folded piece of parchment with forty-seven names. He learned Giant during his captivity, not by choice but by necessity — you learn to understand the language of your captors when your survival depends on anticipating their orders. He knows fire giant culture, fire giant military structure, and fire giant cruelty with the intimate knowledge of a survivor. He does not hate giants. Hatred is an emotion, and Vex does not trade in emotions. He has a debt, and he will pay it. The forty-seven are still in the Cinderworks, and he is coming back for them.
